CHAPTER III · THE CHURCH IN ACTS
The first of the Twelve to die
And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
“Herod the king” kills “James the brother of John with the sword” (Acts 12:1–2).
John son of Zebedee, Herod (Agrippa I)
Tradition, by who said it and when · 3 sources
What Scripture says of his end
When James and John asked for the places of honour, Jesus told them, “Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of” (Mark 10:39).

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword” (Acts 12:1–2). Of the Twelve, he is the only one Scripture says was put to death.
Acts tells his death just before Peter’s arrest, which it sets in “the days of unleavened bread”, and before Herod’s own death at Caesarea (Acts 12:3–4, 19–23).
Camerlynck (1910) dates the death to the Passover of AD 44, the year in which Herod Agrippa I died.

VIEWS, WITH WHO HOLDS THEM · THIS PAGE
Did James preach in Spain before he died?
Writers from the 9th century on (Notker, Walafrid Strabo); defended by the Bollandists
Camerlynck reports the tradition and that the Bollandists defended it in the Acta Sanctorum.
The objections as summarised by A. Camerlynck (1910), who says “numerous scholars reject it”

James died in AD 44 in Jerusalem (Acts 12:2), and early writers say the apostles had not yet left Jerusalem. Paul, planning to visit Spain, says he would not “build upon another man’s foundation” (Rom 15:20, 24). No early writer or council mentions it.
